sop_modules.name: New Drywall Wall Preparation
sop_modules.description: Prepare new drywall wall surfaces for primer application. Includes substrate inspection, defect repair, and dust removal. Inspection/repair intensity is QT-driven. NO spot-priming of fasteners — new drywall fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant (RC-001).

tasks.name: Inspect Wall Surface
tasks.description: Walk all wall surfaces with work light angled to reveal defects: fastener pops, unfilled joints, damaged paper, ridges, screw dimples not fully filled, or debris. Raking light angle is critical — direct overhead light hides wall defects.

quality_notes.QT2: Note only major defects (unfilled joints, fastener pops, holes)
quality_notes.QT3: Identify and mark all visible defects including minor ridges and screw dimples
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive inspection under bright raking light, mark all imperfections including texture inconsistencies

tasks.name: Repair Wall Defects
tasks.description: Fill identified defects with lightweight spackle or joint compound. Sand smooth when dry. Repair intensity is QT-driven. Cross-spec note: if repair is performed here, SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should skip its first inspection/repair round.

quality_notes.QT2: Fill major defects only — holes, unfilled joints
quality_notes.QT3: Fill all marked defects, sand smooth, feather edges
quality_notes.QT4: Thorough repair of all defects, meticulous feathering, uniform surface

cross_spec_flag.description: When this task is completed, SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should skip its first inspection/repair round to avoid double-counting labor.

tasks.name: Vacuum Wall Drywall Dust
tasks.description: Remove drywall dust from wall surfaces using HEPA vacuum with brush attachment. Work top-to-bottom systematically. Walls accumulate more dust than ceilings. Critical for primer adhesion.

quality_notes.all: All surfaces must be dust-free before priming. Dust compromises adhesion at every quality tier.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Repair → Vacuum. Inspection identifies defects, repair addresses them, vacuum removes all dust (including repair dust) before priming. NO spot-priming of fasteners (RC-001).

sop_modules.name: Floor Protection for Wall Roll
sop_modules.description: Set up perimeter floor protection for wall rolling. Roll method has minimal drip risk — perimeter drops along base of walls sufficient.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter)
tasks.description: Position canvas drop cloths along base of walls being rolled. Perimeter coverage for catching drips and roller splatter.

quality_notes.all: Drops positioned along base of all walls being worked. No gaps at corners.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Teardown (Perimeter)
tasks.description: Remove perimeter drop cloths after wall priming is complete. Fold toward center to contain debris.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Setup before rolling. Teardown after all wall prime rolling is complete. In NC sequence, drops may stay for subsequent finish phase.

sop_modules.name: Floor Protection for Wall Spray
sop_modules.description: Set up full-room floor protection before wall spray work. Wall spray overspray falls to floor — full coverage required.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (Full Room)
tasks.description: Install full-room floor protection. Hard floors: rosin paper with taped seams and perimeter tape. Carpet: 1.5 mil plastic with taped edges. Full coverage required — wall spray overspray falls to floor.

quality_notes.all: Full room coverage, all seams taped, no gaps.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Teardown (Full Room)
tasks.description: Remove floor protection after wall spray priming is complete. Fold toward center to contain debris.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Setup before any spray work. Teardown after all wall spray/backroll complete. In NC sequence, floor protection may stay for subsequent phases.

sop_modules.name: Fixture Protection for Wall Spray
sop_modules.description: Remove covers and protect fixtures before wall spray. Uses per-room heuristic (average 6 outlets/switches per room). In NC, fixtures may or may not be installed at prime time.

tasks.name: Remove Outlet Covers, Switch Plates, and HVAC Registers
tasks.description: Remove all outlet covers and switch plates from walls. Remove HVAC register covers and label them for reinstallation. Outlet covers and switch plates are removed, not masked — masking leaves paint edges and doesn't protect properly. HVAC registers are removed and labeled to prevent loss.

quality_notes.all: All covers and registers removed and labeled. Electrical boxes exposed — mask outlet/switch boxes to protect from overspray.

tasks.name: Mask Electrical Boxes and Light Fixtures
tasks.description: Mask exposed outlet boxes and switch boxes with tape to protect from overspray. Light fixtures: loosen from wall or ceiling and mask off with tape/plastic. Do not fully remove light fixtures — loosen and wrap.

quality_notes.all: All electrical boxes masked. Light fixtures loosened and wrapped. No exposed surfaces in overspray zone.

tasks.name: Remove Masking from Boxes and Fixtures
tasks.description: Remove masking from electrical boxes and light fixtures after wall spray priming is complete. Re-seat loosened light fixtures. Do NOT reinstall outlet covers, switch plates, or HVAC registers — they remain off until after finish paint phase.

quality_notes.all: All masking removed. Light fixtures re-seated. Covers and registers remain off for finish paint phase.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove covers/registers → Mask boxes/fixtures before spray. After spray: unmask boxes/fixtures and re-seat lights. Covers and registers are NOT reinstalled during prime — they stay off until after finish paint. In NC, if electrical is not yet installed, this module may be skipped.

sop_modules.name: Apply Wall Primer - Roller Method
sop_modules.description: Apply primer coat to walls using roller with extension pole. Includes cut-in at ceiling edge.

tasks.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge
tasks.description: Brush-cut primer along wall-to-ceiling boundary. Cut line should be clean and extend 2-3 inches down from ceiling for roller overlap. Working at comfortable height for standard walls; step ladder for taller walls.

quality_notes.QT2: Acceptable edge, minor wavering tolerated if coverage complete
quality_notes.QT3: Clean, consistent edge with no visible wobble at distance
quality_notes.QT4: Crisp edge with minimal brush marks, straight line, no visible wobble at 3 feet

tasks.name: Roll Primer on Wall
tasks.description: Apply primer to wall field using 9-inch roller on extension pole. Work in W-pattern, maintain wet edge, avoid lap marks. Wall rolling is at natural standing position — faster and less fatiguing than ceiling work.

quality_notes.all: All tiers: properly painted surface per PCA. No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Surface must be uniformly sealed.

tasks.name: Roll Primer on Wall (Textured Surface)
tasks.description: Apply primer to textured wall surfaces using 3/4-inch nap roller on extension pole. Heavier nap required to work primer into texture valleys. Maintain wet edge.

quality_notes.all: All tiers: properly painted surface per PCA. No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. All texture valleys must be filled and sealed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cut-in first, then roll. Maintain wet edge between cut-in and roll to avoid lap marks at ceiling line.

sop_modules.name: Apply Wall Primer - Spray + Backroll Method
sop_modules.description: Apply primer to walls via airless spray followed by backroll for consolidation and leveling. Backroll is strongly recommended on drywall for consolidation into pores. Backroller sets the pace per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine.

tasks.name: Spray Primer on Wall
tasks.description: Apply primer via airless sprayer. Maintain proper distance, 50% overlap, consistent speed. Work systematically wall by wall. Spray rate is coupled to backroll rate — sprayer cannot outpace backroller.

quality_notes.all: All tiers: properly painted surface per PCA. No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks.

tasks.name: Backroll Sprayed Wall Primer
tasks.description: Immediately follow spray with 18-inch roller on extension pole to consolidate primer into wall surface. Critical for eliminating air pockets and leveling. Backroller sets the production pace.

quality_notes.all: All tiers: properly painted surface per PCA. No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Primer must be fully consolidated into drywall surface.

tasks.name: Cut-In Ceiling Edge After Wall Spray
tasks.description: Touch up ceiling-line edge with brush after spray/backroll. Required if spray coverage at ceiling line is not clean or if primer extended onto ceiling.

quality_notes.QT2: Cover any bleed past ceiling line
quality_notes.QT3: Clean edge, cover any spray overshoot
quality_notes.QT4: Crisp edge, straight line, no visible overshoot

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Spray → Backroll (immediately) → Touch-up cut-in at ceiling. Backroller must follow sprayer closely — spray rate cannot exceed backroll rate per Estimation_Modifiers_Doctrine.

sop_modules.name: Wall Prime Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Clean tools, vacuum floor, and inspect wall prime work.

tasks.name: Vacuum Floor After Wall Prime
tasks.description: Vacuum floor area to remove dust, debris, and any primer drips/overspray from floor protection or exposed floor. Applies regardless of whether floor protection was installed.

quality_notes.all: Floor area clean and free of debris.

tasks.name: Clean Tools
tasks.description: Clean brushes, rollers, spray equipment with water. Store or dispose properly.

tasks.name: Final Wall Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all primed wall surfaces. Check for holidays, missed spots, drips, or edge issues. Use raking light for inspection. Touch up as needed.

quality_notes.QT2: Quick visual check for major misses
quality_notes.QT3: Walk all surfaces, check with raking light, touch up as needed
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive inspection under bright raking light, touch up any visible defects

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Vacuum floor → Clean tools → Final inspect. Clean tools before primer dries.

round_configurations.name: Single Wall Prime Round
round_configurations.description: Standard single coat of primer for new drywall walls.
round_configurations.notes: Single primer coat is standard for new drywall walls with topcoat to follow.

round_configurations.name: Wall Prime (Premium)
round_configurations.description: Premium primer application for QT4 wall finish.
round_configurations.notes: Light sand of primed surface is prep phase of SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH, not part of prime spec.

assumptions.value: No trim masking or trim edge tasks included
assumptions.source: Brief Section 9 — NC sequence, trim not installed during prime
assumptions.note: Trim (baseboard, door casing, window casing) is not installed during wall prime phase in NC. All trim adjacency edge work is deferred to SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH.

assumptions.value: No ceiling-line masking task for spray methods
assumptions.source: Brief Section 9 — ceiling is either bare or being primed simultaneously
assumptions.note: In NC sequence, ceiling is either bare drywall or being primed in same session. No ceiling masking needed during wall prime. This differs from repaint where ceiling_line masking would be required.

exclusions.description: No spot-priming of fasteners — NC fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant (RC-001)
No trim masking tasks — trim is not installed during NC wall prime phase
No ceiling-line masking for spray — ceiling is bare or being primed simultaneously in NC
No furniture protection — new construction is vacant
